title: 基礎熱力学
subtitle: Basic Thermodynamics
keywords: Thermal equilibrium 2.The first law of thermodynamics 3.Thermodynamic process of ideal gas 4.Gas cycle 5.Contribution to local community, IoT
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) Learn basic knowledge of the irreversibility in the nature world (2) Learn how to convert energy and obtain work from heat (3) Acquire design skills for energy conversion in mechanical engineering
advice: Even in advanced mechanical systems, proper energy management is key to their operation and energy efficiency, underscoring thermodynamics as a crucial foundational discipline. Therefore, this course aims to cover the fundamentals of thermodynamics, focusing specifically on the following topics. 1. Definitions of heat, temperature, and systems 2. Thermal equilibrium and the zeroth law of thermodynamics 3. The first law of thermodynamics 4. Equation of state of ideal gases and thermodynamic process of ideal gas 5. Gas cycle The ability to accurately model and simulate the course contents provides a foundation for the use of CAE and AI in design and manufacturing. Students are advised not merely to memorize formulas, but to envision the physical phenomena that the equations represent constantly. Note: This course plan is subject to change. Details will be provided in the first week of class.
books: JSME Textbook Series Thermodynamics ISBN:4-88898-104-3 C3353
requiredKnowledge: Have sufficient skill in mathematics (especially differential and integral calculations). Know how to use a calculator.

Be able to explain gas cycles and apply the knowledge to probrems about design of thermal equipment

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Explain thermal equilibrium, the zeroth law of thermodynamics, heat, temperature, thermodynamic quantities of state, and work. Also, use this understanding to solve advanced problems. (2) Explain the thermal properties of mixed gases. Also, use this understanding to solve advanced problems. (3) Explain the first law of thermodynamics. Also, use this understanding to solve advanced problems related to thermal issues. (4) Explain the thermodynamic process of an ideal gas. Also, evaluate the performance of thermal systems. (5) Explain gas cycles. Also, evaluate the performance of thermal systems.
